what_this_is: Not a verdict. A classification receipt: it records that the leaf below is not a value adjudication, so the dissenting verdict filed against it does not stand as a finding about the tree. R-15's 2026-08-14 amendment rules that a membership transition which is the ruled consequence of a declared change is adjudicated by CITATION, not by verdict, and this is that citation.
rules: R-15, amended 2026-08-14 (docs/plans/silent-failure-runbook.md, *Independent investigation*): adjudicated by citation, not by verdict; both guards checked below.

R-19 / the R-15/R-18 amendment's adjudication clause 3: a superseding receipt names the specific defect in the brief it replaces and names what it supersedes; the superseded receipt is never edited and never deleted.

category_error.name: ruled field removal
category_error.one_sentence: `owner` is present on a cross-participant packet IFF its Authority is SPLIT (D-07), so the field's absence is what a landed authority ruling says -- not a number an oracle can weigh.
category_error.detail: D-07's check is: every packet modifying another participant's damage declares an Authority, and `owner` is present iff Authority == SPLIT. The Phase 4 S7 Bloodsong move takes bloodsong.expose_weakness off SPLIT, so its three armings in this scenario carry no owner, while Black Cleaver -- Carve, which is H1-blocked and still SPLIT, keeps its own owner on every row in the same list. An investigator asked whether `main` is the right value for that field has no evidence that can answer: cached wiki text describes what Expose Weakness does, never which engine the campaign ruled owns it.

leaves_reclassified.superseded_confidence_as_filed: low-moderate -- 'this leaf is a provenance/serialization field, not a game quantity, and no wiki text or documented formula fixes its value', the receipt's own words

defect_in_the_prior_brief.clause: R-19 / adjudication clause 3 -- a re-run or a supersession must cite the specific defect in the brief it replaces.
defect_in_the_prior_brief.defect: The brief posed a ruled provenance field as a value question, and R-19's closed verdict set left no way to say so: the investigator reconstructed both items from cached wiki text, concluded correctly that every support effect in the scenario is emitted BY a roster participant, and mapped that onto `old_value_correct` -- a dissent meaning 'no evidence exists' filed in the same shape as one meaning 'the tree is wrong'. Its own confidence line says as much. The brief was underdetermined in a second way it could not see: the leaf was addressed by ordinal, and support_events[17] is a Black Cleaver -- Carve arming in the pre-change list and a Bloodsong -- Expose Weakness arming in the post-change one, so the pair `main -> <absent>` straddled two different records.
defect_in_the_prior_brief.recorded_as: escalated-defects-S6S7-oracle.json::the_verdict_enum_has_no_member_for_a_leaf_the_evidence_tree_cannot_decide, which names this receipt by id and already states that its absence is D-07's ruled consequence of the authority move.

the_instrument_fix.what: scripts/golden_snapshot.py::leaf_report pairs list members carrying event_id by that identity and never by list position.

measured_after.what_the_ordinal_was_hiding: The pre-change record at ordinal 17, enemy:Aatrox:support:17, is a Black Cleaver -- Carve arming that the S7 rearm fold no longer authors; it is now reported as its own removal at /coupled_scenarios/cleaver_bloodsong_roster/combat/support_events[17]. The owner drop belongs to the Expose Weakness arming the baseline holds at ordinal 18.
measured_after.the_sibling_armings: The same drop is reported at support_events[5]/owner (enemy:Aatrox:support:0) and support_events[12]/owner (enemy:Aatrox:support:1) -- the two Expose Weakness armings no removal shifted -- and both are claimed by expected-golden-diff-P4-S7-bloodsong.json. Three armings, one ruled consequence, and only the third one was ever routed to an oracle.
measured_after.how_measured: scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json, read through tests/test_coupled_golden_allowlist.py::standing_coupled_diffs on this tip.

ruling_cited.ruling: D-07 -- every packet modifying another participant's damage declares an Authority, and `owner` is present iff Authority == SPLIT -- applied to the Phase 4 S7 Bloodsong authority move.
openable_at: docs/plans/2026-08-08-silent-failure-campaign.md -- D-07 in the D-01…D-14 table, and Amendment D for the member the move landed
docs/receipts/expected-golden-diff-P4-S7-bloodsong.json -- the slice receipt, which already claims the same drop at support_events[5]/owner and support_events[12]/owner
ruling_cited.why_it_decides_the_leaf: The field's presence is the decision's own consequence: keep the owner and the packet contradicts its declared authority; drop it and the packet says what the ruling says. There is no third value to be right about.

guards.note: The transition is value_to_absent on a record both sides hold, matched by identity -- so it is a field the ruling removed, not a value re-spelled as a removal by an ordinal shift, which the pre-fix report could not distinguish.

effect.on_the_leaf: It is no longer an open value adjudication and owes no oracle receipt.
effect.on_the_entry: escalated-defects-S6S7-oracle.json::the_verdict_enum_has_no_member_for_a_leaf_the_evidence_tree_cannot_decide stays OPEN. The amendment answers one of the two options its for_the_owner named, and only for the subclass a ruling decides: a membership transition produced by a declared change is now adjudicated by citation instead of being routed to an oracle at all. Its second citation, oracle-S6S7-leaf30 on an event's `sequence`, is engine bookkeeping that no ruling removed and no evidence tree can decide, so the gap the entry names is narrowed, not closed.
effect.on_the_baselines: None. No baseline moves in the commit that lands this (R-17, R-32, D-97).
effect.on_the_thirteen_boundary_dissents: None. C4 is the S6/S7 ledger's, not the boundary's.
